shared_conventions.speed: speed_wpm = natural English words per minute (designed per character). speed_cpm = the pipeline field used by code/check_dialogue_fit.py (est_s = eff_chars / (speed_cpm_mid/60), eff_chars = letters+digits only, no spaces/punctuation). Conversion: speed_cpm = round(speed_wpm x 3.8), where 3.8 = measured mean letters+digits per word over all 10,739 dialogue words (40,974 eff chars) in structured_story ch001-ch012. Example: 150 wpm -> 570 cpm.
shared_conventions.acoustic_fields: gender / pitch / timbre / accent are pure acoustic descriptions (English) because genmedia seed-audio-1.0 concatenates them verbatim into the voice-design prompt. Story context, sources and staging notes live only in reference_style / emotion_range notes / voice_evidence / reason.
shared_conventions.gender: copied verbatim from each appearance.json (male/female). Ensembles copy the appearance majority gender; mixed-gender members are specified per slot in group_voice.speaking_slots (voice-generation: sample the card's lead voice; per-slot voices are text descriptions for prompt/TTS library).
shared_conventions.pitch_range_hz: indicative F0 band for the voice at rest-to-peak; pitch_delta values in emotion_range are semitones relative to baseline.
shared_conventions.accent_policy: 1862 England near Oxford: Alice, her sister and the educated/court figures in Received Pronunciation (upper/upper-middle class); tradesmen and servants in class/regional accents — Pat rural Irish brogue (source: 'arrum', 'yer honour', ch004-p19); Gryphon London Cockney (sourced dialect grammar); Hatter light London tradesman; gardeners, cook, Bill and the ch004 crowd rural Oxfordshire working-class burr.
shared_conventions.SUP-002: all dream figures are human performers: no animal noises, no pitch-shifting or creature processing. Animal-coding shows only as human vocal colour (Frog-Footman croak, Cat purr-soft delivery). SUP-003: Alice's voice is never processed for size changes.
shared_conventions.native_audio: dialogue is native video-model audio (no TTS in the final film); these cards feed voice-generation voiceprint samples (3-5s reference_audio anchors) and the dialogue TTS library for animatics only.

voice_collision_design: Same-scene speakers were separated by pitch band + texture + tempo: Hatter (quick reedy tenor, London) vs March Hare (slower breathy baritone) vs Dormouse (slow husky murmur); Queen (brassy alto->shrill) vs King (soft fussy light baritone) vs White Rabbit (thin reedy high tenor) vs Knave (smooth level baritone); Gryphon (hoarse Cockney bass-baritone) vs Mock Turtle (hollow genteel sobbing bass); Duchess (hoarse growling contralto) vs Cook (flat monotone low alto); Frog-Footman (croaky low monotone) vs Fish-Footman (dry thin tenor-baritone); Alice (clear ~10yo girl, RP) vs Eaglet (thinner scratchier 8-9yo) vs sister (warm mezzo, slower); gardeners Two/Five/Seven stepped low/mid/high.
